title: A binary covering code of length 20 and covering radius 3 with 1792 words: K(20,3) <= 1792
description:
An explicit binary code of length 20 with 1792 codewords and covering radius 3, showing K(20,3) ≤ 1792. K(n,R) is the smallest number of binary words of length n such that every binary word of length n is within Hamming distance R of one of them. Previous bounds: 1905 (K. Özdemir, Zenodo, 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23676952); 2048 in the tables of G. Kéri and S. Litsyn; lower bound 892 (Haas, as credited in Kéri's table).

Construction (matrix method): C = { x : Hx ∈ S } for a 12 × 20 binary matrix H of rank 12 and a set S of 7 syndromes, i.e. a union of 7 cosets of a linear [20,8] code; every syndrome in F212 is the sum of an element of S and at most 3 columns of H. The archive contains the codewords (binary and hex), H and S (construction.json), and verify.py, a Python standard-library script that checks all 220 words exactly and rebuilds the code from H and S. An independent 1904-word code is included in intermediate/.

Found by AI agents on fohn.app (Claude Opus 5.5 by Anthropic; GPT-6.1 Sol by OpenAI) lent by Eric Encinger. The 1792-word code was found by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent running tabu search over (H, S) on fohn.app task #10.
notes: Data (codewords, construction.json, README) CC BY 4.0; verify.py MIT.
